title: Legacy flat / B1 closure audit before Track 1 paper

1_legacy_file_book_flat.note: carries a breaker block: system_equity 50408.25 against last_broker_equity 996730.93 — the account is far larger than the epoch this route sizes from

2_broker_flat.how: IBKRBroker read-only on client id 97 — the class the safety jobs already use. get_positions() (ib.positions(), unfiltered, retry-until-stable) and get_open_orders() (reqAllOpenOrders, ALL clients, None-not-empty on failure).
2_broker_flat.corroboration: the dashboard's own reader on client id 99 reported the same 0/0 and equity 996883.66 — two client ids, two code paths, one answer
2_broker_flat.attribution: not needed. Attribution only matters when something is NONZERO; zero positions and zero working orders is unambiguous however many routes share the login. That is the one shape of B1 a shared account can answer.

3_orphan_orders.why: there are no working orders at all, so no order can be orphaned and no position can be naked — there are no positions either

5_can_b1_be_closed_by_measurement.gate: STILL OPEN — and that is correct
5_can_b1_be_closed_by_measurement.why: B1 is a DECISION about which route owns the login. Proving the account flat at 06:15 does not stop legacy opening a position at 14:05, and no measurement can. The gate now requires BOTH: the operator's recorded decision AND a passing measurement. Before this stage it required only the signature.

6_what_remains_for_b1: the operator records the choice in track1_go_live_confirmation.json — either legacy_retired_confirmed or separate_account_confirmed
the B1 audit must have a PASS newer than 24h at the moment the gate is read (re-run `python -m global_index.b1_audit --broker ibkr --record`)

did: read every working order across all clients

8_runtime_or_live_file_changed.written: global_index/track1_b1/track1_b1_20260826.jsonl — the audit's own evidence record, created by --record

11_before_a_tiny_paper_probe.item: THE ORDER PATH ITSELF — run_shadow constructs NoOrderBroker unconditionally and IBKRBroker is never constructed in that module. No code on this route can place an order.

the_defect_that_made_the_cheap_path_unus.shape: both collectors build their list inside try/except; the handler logs a warning and leaves the list EMPTY, and the payload is then published with connected: true and error: null
the_defect_that_made_the_cheap_path_unus.consequence: an empty positions/orders list meant EITHER 'the account holds nothing' OR 'the call raised', with no way to tell — fail-open, on the exact question B1 asks. The dashboard has been showing 0/0 all along and that 0/0 was never decision-grade.
the_defect_that_made_the_cheap_path_unus.fixed: positions_ok / orders_ok / per-section error now travel on the payload; both start False; both are cleared when the connection drops so a stale True cannot keep testifying
the_defect_that_made_the_cheap_path_unus.needs: a backend restart before the snapshot path can answer B1. Until then the audit must be run with --broker ibkr.

a_method_written_in_5X_that_had_no_calle.contract: None when it cannot testify, never []; not filtered by clientId, because an order placed by another client is still exposure on this account
a_method_written_in_5X_that_had_no_calle.note: its docstring names Stage 5U's shared-account finding. The honest reader existed for a year of stages and nothing asked it anything.

the_legacy_trade_log_cannot_prove_flatne.the_suspicious_block: 6 MES SHORT 'OPEN' rows on entry_day 2026-08-07 at 19:10, 19:20, 19:30, 19:40, 19:50 and 20:01 UTC — ten minutes apart, every one with order_id null and perm_id null. Six identical opens at a ten-minute cadence is a job re-logging, not six fills.
the_legacy_trade_log_cannot_prove_flatne.so: 18 OPEN rows are not 18 positions, and the log stops 13 days before the book was last written. The BOOK and the BROKER are the authorities here; the trade log is not evidence of flatness in either direction.
the_legacy_trade_log_cannot_prove_flatne.related: the known exit-path gap — three of five close paths book money and write no trade-log row, which is why exit_path_coverage reads MAX_HOLD = 0

a_check_in_the_runbook_that_can_never_fa.so: the path it forbids is one the code never writes, so that line can never fire
a_check_in_the_runbook_that_can_never_fa.and_substantively: the book is now EXPECTED in shadow — Stage 5ZN gave it the cross-day breaker/day state — so the test is `positions: []`, not absence

two_things_caught_in_my_own_work.an_unreachable_branch: measure() had a `position_without_stop` result that could never be returned: any nonzero broker position fails on the line above it. An unreachable branch reads, to anyone auditing the table, as a check that runs. The status was removed; the detection survives as a FINDING on the broker-positions failure.
two_things_caught_in_my_own_work.the_live_frame_gate_closed_on_me: the audit tool was first written as global_index/track1_b1_audit.py, and the live-frame gate — which scans every global_index/track1_*.py for IBKRBroker and requires the splice guard — shut immediately. A FOURTH blocker appeared. The gate was right; the file was in the wrong category. It moved to global_index/b1_audit.py beside run_stop_repair and run_maxhold_exit, which connect to IBKR and are outside that namespace for the same reason. The gate was not touched, and a test pins both directions.

gate_change.after: signed AND (measurement passes OR an explicit waiver flag is set)
gate_change.direction: strictly tighter — a signature alone no longer opens it
gate_change.new_field: Blocker.also_requires_measurement (an AND, where released_by_measurement is an OR) plus Blocker.waiver_flag
gate_change.waiver: b1_measurement_waived — releases NOTHING on its own, and load_confirmations refuses it without a `note` saying why the account could not be asked
gate_change.unchanged_for_everything_else: every other blocker has both new fields empty, asserted
gate_change.self_check: clean; two new structural rules added (a waiver with nothing to waive, and a flag that would bypass itself)

tests.style: structured payloads and AST; no prose greps

mutations.guard: the harness checks pytest actually COLLECTED tests — an exit code of 5 means nothing ran, and reading that as red is how a sweep certifies itself

a_stale_pin_found_in_a_suite_no_regressi.why_not: the whole Track 1 panel is uncommitted work on this branch, so there is no earlier revision to compare against. Which stage pluralised the label cannot be established and is not guessed at.
a_stale_pin_found_in_a_suite_no_regressi.what_is_measurable: this suite was in no stage's regression set, so whichever stage renamed it, nothing was watching
a_stale_pin_found_in_a_suite_no_regressi.fixed: the label list corrected AND completed — it pinned 10 of the 13 facts the panel renders, so three could have vanished unnoticed. A second test now checks the other direction.

claims_deliberately_NOT_made: that Track 1 is ready for paper
that the account will still be flat later today
that the trade log proves anything about flatness
that the dashboard's 0/0 was evidence before the reader fix

full_scratch_sweep.note: the same 14 suites run ALONE give 28 failures, so 15 of the 43 are order-dependent — cross-suite state leakage, a separate problem this stage did not chase

bisect.method: every 5ZQ edit reverted and both new modules moved aside, in a subprocess, then the same 14 suites re-run and everything restored and digest-verified
bisect.why: 5ZQ gave the method its first caller. The test's NAME says nothing in the LEGACY ROUTE calls it; its ASSERTION said nothing ANYWHERE does — a stronger claim than the intent behind it, and the reason the method sat uncalled for several stages. It now names its allowed callers, still fails on any unnamed one, and a second test requires the allowed caller to actually call it.

twenty_six_tests_were_already_red_and_no.measured: reverting every 5ZQ change leaves 26 of the 27 failing — they predate this stage. The baseline this stage recorded at 06:03 ET proves the two biggest causes independently: three blockers, and live_positions.track1.json already on disk from the 02:55 NKD close.

categories_diagnosed.roster pins: tests assert the EXACT blocker list — one blocker, then two. Stale since Stage 5S added PAPER_SHADOW_EVIDENCE and 5ZL added REGIME_LABEL_VERIFICATION. None of these tests is ABOUT the roster; pinning it means every new blocker breaks unrelated suites.
categories_diagnosed.absence proxies: tests assert live_positions.track1.json does not exist. Stale since Stage 5ZN deliberately gave the route a cross-day book. Same defect as the runbook line above.
categories_diagnosed.slot-count pins: tests expect 25 Track 1 slots and 'the two windows'. Stale since Stage 5N gave the route all four sleeves (70 strategy slots).
categories_diagnosed.substring-over-prose: ONE test reported 'a Track 1 slot asks for orders' — matching a COMMENT in the slot builder that says *Still no --allow-orders*. The comment asserting the absence read as the presence.

twenty_six_tests_were_already_red_and_no.not_diagnosed: the two in 5ZO and the three in 5Z-freshness were not traced. Saying which stage stranded them would be a guess.
repaired_here_and_why: the substring-over-prose one — a red test claiming a shadow slot can request orders is the one alarm nobody should have to re-derive, and it was false
one roster pin, rewritten to assert its own claim (orders impossible, B1 among the reasons) instead of the roster — which is the repair the whole family needs
twenty_six_tests_were_already_red_and_no.deliberately_left: the other 24. Fixing them is a stage of its own, and doing it half way inside this one would be worse than naming them precisely.
twenty_six_tests_were_already_red_and_no.recommended: a dedicated sweep: stop pinning rosters, replace absence proxies with mtime-vs-import, and add scratch/ to the regression set some stage runs
